title: Degradation Amphitheater: Operator Playbook for Tiered Fallbacks
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:
This runbook defines the 'Degradation Amphitheater' — a staged operator playbook and decision ladder for handling multi-tenant LLM inference degradations that progress through observable tiers. The amphitheater metaphor maps signals and operator interventions to concentric response rings: detection, containment, mitigation, and recovery.

Scope:
- Services: platform-router, inference-runtime, kv-prefix-cache, batch-allocator, tenant-slicer
- Regions: all production regions (us-west1, eu-central1)
- Audience: platform operators, on-call engineers, SRE leads

Intent:
- Provide a compact, repeatable decision ladder for multi-signal degradations (latency, token errors, cache thrash, tail-latency).
- Minimize blast radius with progressive interventions that preserve SLAs for priority tenants.
- Capture operator actions, dashboard views, and post-incident hygiene steps.

Owner and Escalation:
- Primary owner: Platform SRE (rotation: platform-oncall@redwood)
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime team
- Escalation path: oncall -> platform-sre lead -> runtime engineering -> product incident commander

SLOs and Thresholds (reference):
- Global P95 token-latency target: 1200ms
- SLO burn alert: 15% burn in 1h -> Pager
- Critical customer latency SLA (reserved capacity): P95 <= 500ms -> SEV if violated for >15m

Detection (observability anchors):
- Primary signals (alert rules):
  1) token-latency-p95 > 1200ms for 10m (dashboard: Token Latency Overview -> panel id: token-latency-p95)
  2) inference-runtime-5xx-rate > 0.5% for 5m
  3) kv-prefix-cache-fill-ratio drop > 30% over 5m (sign of eviction storm)
  4) burst-cold-start-rate > 2x baseline for 15m
- Secondary signals: tenant error rate increase, queue-depth skew, allocation rejections, GPU preemption events

Decision Ladder (rings):
1) Ring 0 — Observe (no operator action):
   - Actions: annotate incident in pager, open triage channel (#platform-degradation)
   - Key checks: verify metric spike, confirm signal source (region/model/tenant)
2) Ring 1 — Contain (automated soft mitigations + operator light-touch)
   - When: single-region or single-model P95 spikes; burn < 10%
   - Automated steps: enable conservative batching override (if configured), increase prefix-KV cache TTL for hot keys by +25% via feature-flag
   - Operator steps: reduce non-critical background prefetch cohorts (CLI: platform-prefetch cohort disable --cohort-id=<id>)
3) Ring 2 — Mitigate (operator-driven config changes)
   - When: multi-region signal or SLO burn > 10% sustained 15m; tenant-impact visible
   - Actions (ordered):
     a) Route low-priority traffic to degraded-capacity model variant (routing DSL):
        - CLI example: redwood route apply --from=prod-model:v1 --to=prod-model:v1-degraded --filter=tenant_priority<=low
     b) Trigger soft-eviction of large KV shards to rebalance (operator tool):
        - CLI: kv-shard-evict --shard-id=<id> --grace-period=30s --owner=platform-oncall
     c) Temporarily thottle bursty tenants: update tenant soft-quota (API):
        - PATCH /api/tenants/<tenant>/quota {"burst_factor":0.5}
4) Ring 3 — Critical (immediate protective actions)
   - When: SLO burn >= 15% or 2+ critical customers impacted for >10m
   - Actions:
     - Initiate emergency model-swap to a smaller footprint quantized variant (runtime command)
     - Disable non-essential observability sampling that adds CPU contention (follow checklist)
     - Consider regional traffic evacuation: divert new requests to healthy region using traffic-stitching runbook

Operator Playbook (step-by-step checklist):
1) Triage:
   - Open investigation doc in incident workspace (title: Degradation Amphitheater - <region> - <time>)
   - Record initial signals and dashboards viewed (list panels and query snippets)
2) Correlate:
   - Run: grafana query "A: token_latency_p95{region=~\"us-.*\"}" and compare with GPU-metrics
   - Check allocation logs: kubectl logs -n runtime allocator-controller --since=1h | grep "rejected"
3) Contain (if entering Ring 1):
   - Toggle prefetch cohorts: platform-prefetch cohort set --cohort=<id> --state=paused
   - Increase KV TTL: feature-flag set kv.cache.ttl.hot_keys_multiplier=1.25
4) Mitigate (if entering Ring 2):
   - Apply routing override for low-priority tenants
   - Execute shard-eviction for top-3 eviction hotspots
   - Patch tenant soft-quotas for noisy tenants (document reason and owner)
5) Critical (if Ring 3):
   - Run emergency model swap: runtime model swap --from <model> --to <degraded-model> --region <region>
   - Notify customers via CS-incident template and trigger SEV call if enterprise customers affected

Safe-guards and Safety Checks:
- All change commands have a required rollback window (operator CLI prompts).
- Any routing or model-swap must include a canary window (5 minutes) and automated rollback on error rate regressions.
- If performing shard eviction, monitor kv-consistency-check endpoint.

Dashboards and Panels to open (minimum):
- Token Latency Overview (p95, p99) — panel ids: token-latency-p95, token-latency-p99
- KV Prefix Cache Health — panel ids: kv-eviction-rate, kv-fill-ratio
- Allocation and Eviction — allocator-accept-rate, allocator-rejects
- Tenant Impact Map — tenant-latency-heatmap

Alert Mappings and Pager Guidance:
- token-latency-p95-alert -> Platform oncall Pager (severity: P3)
- inference-runtime-5xx -> Platform oncall Pager (severity: P2)
- kv-eviction-storm -> Platform lead (severity: P2)
- enterprise-sla-violation -> SEV (severity: P1)

Rollback Recipes:
- Revert routing override: redwood route rollback --id=<override-id>
- Re-enable prefetch cohorts: platform-prefetch cohort set --cohort=<id> --state=active
- Rehydrate KV shards (if safe): kv-shard-rehydrate --shard-id=<id> --from-backup=true

Post-Incident Hygiene (must do within 48h):
1) Incident write-up: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, metrics pre/post, owner for each action
2) Action items: label with owner and ETA in ticket queue (triage board)
3) Metrics baselining: capture 72h before/after heatmaps for token-latency, evictions, and allocation rejects
4) Safety changes: add automated rollbacking hooks where manual overrides were used more than once

Retrospective template (short):
- Summary: what happened, where, and impact (customers affected, SLO burn)
- Root cause analysis: primary trigger, contributing factors
- Timeline: detection -> containment -> mitigation -> recovery with timestamps and commands executed
- Remediation plan: short-term fixes (<=2w), medium (<=3mo), long-term architecture changes
- Owner signoffs and verification steps

Appendices:
- Common CLI snippets (already embedded above)
- Grafana query examples:
  - token-latency-p95 by model: sum by (model) (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])))
- Checklists for safe model swap and traffic diversion (operator must sign-off in incident doc)

Notes and design rationale:
- The amphitheater approach prioritizes small, reversible interventions near the outer rings to limit operator cognitive load and reduce churn. Inner rings are reserved for high-confidence and high-impact actions that require coordination.

Related reading and links:

- Warm start strategy and soft eviction runbook (see related_pages)
